root_cause.text: In `rxrpc_input_packet_on_conn()` the client-side implicit-end protocol error path unconditionally decremented a call reference even when `rxrpc_try_get_call()` had returned NULL because `chan->call` was already torn down, causing an invalid `rxrpc_put_call()` on a non-acquired reference.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `rxrpc_put_call(call, rxrpc_call_put_input);` to `if (call) rxrpc_put_call(call, rxrpc_call_put_input);`, and the commit message explicitly states that `chan->call is NULL, rxrpc_try_get_call() returns NULL and there is no reference to drop`, but the error path “unconditionally calls rxrpc_put_call()”.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a NULL check before dropping the call in the client unexpected-implicit-end path to prevent an invalid call release.
intent_record.what: Inside rxrpc_input_packet_on_conn(), the unconditional rxrpc_put_call(call, rxrpc_call_put_input); in the rxrpc_to_client(sp) branch was replaced with a null check so the call is only released if call is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents dereferencing or releasing a NULL call pointer in the unexpected-implicit-end error path for client packets, while preserving the protocol error return.

grouping_result.intent: Add a NULL check before dropping the call in the client unexpected-implicit-end path to prevent an invalid call release.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds a NULL check in the client implicit-end error path so `rxrpc_put_call()` is not called when `rxrpc_try_get_call()` returned NULL, preventing the invalid reference drop.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional call release is the root cause: in the client unexpected-implicit-end path it could execute even when rxrpc_try_get_call() had returned NULL, leading to an invalid put on a non-acquired reference.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally releases the call reference in the client unexpected-implicit-end path. If rxrpc_try_get_call() had returned NULL because chan->call was already torn down, executing this rxrpc_put_call() would operate on a non-acquired reference, which is the reported vulnerability.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable pattern is present in the client-side implicit-end path. The code does `call = rxrpc_try_get_call(rcu_dereference(chan->call), rxrpc_call_get_input);` and then, when `sp->hdr.callNumber > chan->call_id` and `rxrpc_to_client(sp)` is true, it unconditionally executes `rxrpc_put_call(call, rxrpc_call_put_input);` before `goto reject_packet;` (lines 370-374). This is exactly the dangerous construct described: if `rxrpc_try_get_call()` returned NULL because `chan->call` was already torn down, the unconditional put would act on a non-acquired reference. There is no NULL guard before the put in this branch, so the fix is not present in this function body.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described is the client-side implicit-end path that unconditionally decremented a call reference after `rxrpc_try_get_call()` had failed. In this diff, that pattern is no longer present. The code now explicitly guards the call ref acquisition with `if (call && !rxrpc_try_get_call(call, rxrpc_call_get_input)) call = NULL;`, and later only does `rxrpc_put_call(call, rxrpc_call_put_input);` after `rxrpc_input_call_event(call, skb);` when `call` is non-NULL. Also, the implicit-end handling was changed from `if (call) rxrpc_input_implicit_end_call(rx, conn, call); call = NULL;` to `if (call) { rxrpc_input_implicit_end_call(conn, call); chan->call = NULL; call = NULL; }`, so the function avoids dereferencing or putting a call that was never successfully acquired. This snippet is sufficient to determine the fix is present and the specific bug is absent.
